subject: Equinox priority feature ask: audit-export hooks + routing affinity
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Equinox priority feature ask: audit-export hooks + routing affinity

Team —

Quick context: Equinox (large payments customer, deal EQX-4387) sign is contingent on two product items we do not currently surface in the roadmap: (1) a scheduled audit-export hook (near-real-time CSV/Parquet push or SFTP deliverable of per-request metadata and redaction logs) and (2) routing affinity so their high-volume embedding requests go to a pinned quantized model variant with a strict latency SLA during business hours.

Customer timeline: they want both capabilities in place for pilot kickoff 2027-04-20. Commercially they are asking for a 12-month committed reserved capacity (mid-six figures ARR) if we can commit to the pilot window. Ben is willing to move on commercial concessions if we can give a concrete engineering scope and delivery timeline.

Asks:
- Product: can we scope a minimal audit-export hook (CSV+SFTP endpoint + retention options) that surfaces request_id, timestamp, model, tokens_in/out, redaction_flags, and a link to the full trace? Minimal schema attached.
- Eng: what is the rough effort for routing affinity (per-account model pinning + fallback rules) and the p99 latency guardrails we can guarantee on quantized variants?
- CS (Monica): can you confirm acceptance criteria from the customer side for the audit export (format, delivery cadence) and priority during the pilot?

I know this is a tight window — asking for an initial feasibility note and a ballpark estimate by EOD tomorrow so Ben can align commercial. If this is clearly multi-sprint, say so and provide an earliest realistic milestone.

Thanks,
Marcus
---

Subject: Re: Equinox priority feature ask: audit-export hooks + routing affinity

Marcus — thanks for the clear ask and attachments. Initial read: both items are well-aligned with platform roadmap themes (observability/export and routing/pinning), but they differ in complexity. High-level notes below.

1) Audit-export hook (minimal):
- Scope candidate: scheduled export job that emits a compressed CSV/Parquet to a customer SFTP or signed pre-signed S3 URL. Includes the fields you listed + per-request trace_id.
- Security: must include customer-managed encryption at rest and optional trimming of PII columns (we'll default to redaction flags rather than removing content).
- Effort: I would estimate ~3–4 engineer-weeks to implement the backend export pipeline + basic UI for scheduling + tests. That assumes we reuse existing export infra components.

2) Routing affinity + latency guardrail for quantized embedding model:
- Routing affinity (per-account pin): medium complexity (routing table + policy DSL + rollout safety).
- Guarantee: making a commercial SLA for p99 under burst will require capacity reservation + autoscaling hooks per-tenant (ties into Dedicated flows).
- Effort: rough estimate 6–10 engineer-weeks for a safe MVP (no hard SLA) if we can accept best-effort latency; 12–16 engineer-weeks if customer requires guaranteed p99 SLAs and dedicated capacity changes.

Constraints & options:
- Fast path: implement audit-export MVP + a soft-routing affinity (pinning preference without hard guarantees) in one sprint (4–6 weeks). That would meet the pilot for the export and give them affinity behavior, but we cannot promise a p99 SLA.
- Full path: pinning + guaranteed p99 requires us to provision dedicated capacity lines or an enterprise routing tier; that'll push to a multi-sprint deliverable.

Irene
Irene Choi
Director, Product Management, Redwood Inference

Thanks all for the quick turn. Summary and proposed next steps (please reply inline if you disagree):

Summary:
- Audit-export MVP: agreed scope = compressed CSV/Parquet export to SFTP or S3 presigned URL; includes schema in attachment. Target: 3–4 engineer-weeks.
- Routing affinity: agreed approach = soft pin (routing preference + documented fallback) shipped as a behavioral feature. No p99 SLA for pilot. Target: ship soft-pin behavior in parallel if Karthik confirms scope fits a single 2-week sprint.
- Commercial: Ben will present pilot SOW (implementation fee + reserved capacity) if product/eng can commit to audit-export MVP and routing soft-pin for pilot.

Next steps:
1) Karthik: confirm by EOD tomorrow whether routing soft-pin can be scoped to one 2-week sprint (include required code owners and risk notes).
2) Irene: confirm necessary compliance checklist items for audit-export (encryption/KMS, PII redaction defaults) and whether the MVP needs a UI flow or can be API-only for pilot.
3) Monica: confirm acceptance criteria with Equinox and upload a signed pilot SOW to the HubSpot deal page.
4) Ben: hold commercial terms flexible pending engineering confirmation; will aim to lock SOW by 2027-03-05 EOB.

Looping in the customer so they're aware of the plan — Samantha, Liam: we'll follow up after the internal alignment call tomorrow. Appreciate the team's flexibility.

Marcus
